indicators.note: a variety is a different form or arrangement, so the letters of the two words before are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone describes a range of medical or laboratory tests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a variety of' rearranges TESTS plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: A state is a condition or situation, as in 'a state of disrepair'.

definitions.meaning: to put off is to disconcert or fluster someone
to project something is to hurl or fling it

explanation.definitionFit: Throwing someone means disconcerting them; throwing a ball means hurling or projecting it.

parts.note: a golfer hitting a drive from the tee at the eighteenth hole is starting play there

explanation.walkthrough: 18 looks like an age, as if someone has just passed a driving test; it is the eighteenth hole, and 18-across (GOLF CLUB) shares the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course, the first drive at each hole is played from the tee.

clue.text: Mark added for being absolutely correct

parts.note: a mark or blemish is a spot
something added is put on, as in 'tack on'

explanation.surface: A teacher awards an extra mark because an answer was perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is a British idiom for exactly right or precise.

parts.note: the word draw is the word ward going the other way, so the instruction to make it is to take ward the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Someone is unwilling to follow an art teacher's direction to sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, the answer says: take WARD the other way, which gives DRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Backward can mean shy or hesitant, slow to come forward.

clue.text: Began in absurdly bad way to raise cash for charity

definitions.text: way to raise cash for charity
definitions.note: a noun phrase: a means of fundraising

indicators.note: letters in a bad state are disordered, so the three words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A charity fundraiser got off to a ridiculously poor start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges the fifteen letters of BEGAN IN ABSURDLY; 'way to' completes the definition. A BRING-AND-BUY SALE is a British fundraising event where people donate items and buy others'.
explanation.definitionFit: Such sales are a common British charity fundraiser held in church halls and schools.

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it, so the first comes before the second

parts.note: a con is a swindle or fraud
Crete is a Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A genuine swindle has taken place on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete means actual or tangible, existing in solid fact.

parts.note: a card is a joker or wit, also called a wag
something carried, such as a coat worn, is on

explanation.surface: A playing card is brought along in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a four-wheeled cart for carrying goods.

clue.text: Flee in car, crashing into barrier!

indicators.note: a car crashing is wrecked, so the letters of the three words before are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A getaway driver crashes into a roadside barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence made of horizontal rails is a type of barrier around a field.

clue.text: Reparation made by the old guard

indicators.note: the word Reparation is made into something else by rearranging it

explanation.surface: Compensation is paid by conservative old-timers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges REPARATION; 'the old guard' is literal, Rome's imperial bodyguard, not today's conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: The Praetorian Guard was the emperor's bodyguard in ancient Rome, so a praetorian is a member of it.

definitions.meaning: a bag carried when travelling, an old-fashioned holdall
a hold or firm mastery over something

explanation.definitionFit: A grip is a travelling bag; to have a grip on something is to have control of it.

clue.text: A number written by pen for the last act

indicators.note: a song written by someone is theirs, so the writer's name comes first

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
a number is a song or piece of music

explanation.surface: A tune composed with a fountain pen for a play's final act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool; it is a female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: A swansong is a final performance or achievement before retirement, from the legend that swans sing before dying.

parts.note: to run copies is to print them, as in a print run
food gone rotten is off

explanation.surface: Someone tells a printer to issue a poor reproduction.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off copies is to print and so issue them.

clue.text: A great man she objectively put before love

parts.note: the pronoun she in the objective case is her
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman puts her love second to an admired man.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is a man admired for great deeds.

indicators.note: the start of the next word means only its first letter is used

parts.note: the vocative is the grammatical case used to address someone

explanation.surface: An exciting suitcase has a thrilling opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a box or legal matter; it is a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: Evocative means arousing strong feelings or memories, so stirring.

indicators.note: examining the letters again in another order rearranges them

explanation.surface: A student's grade was beaten when the script was marked again.
explanation.definitionFit: Nota bene is Latin for 'note well', a written prompt to pay attention.

clue.text: Produced some nonsense propagated about Turner

indicators.note: the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: plants or animals propagated are bred
a lathe is a machine that turns wood or metal

explanation.surface: Someone spread rubbish about the painter J.M.W. Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter J.M.W. Turner; it is a machine that turns wood, and 'about' wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: To blather is to talk at length without making sense.

clue.text: Careless fielders keep getting left out

parts.note: slips are close catching positions in cricket, behind the batsman

indicators.note: a letter left out is removed from the word

parts.note: to keep something is to hold it

explanation.surface: Sloppy cricket fielders keep letting the ball go to their left.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIPS are cricket fielders standing beside the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod means sloppy or done without care.

clue.text: Driver hit back with stout stick

indicators.note: the word for hit is read backwards

parts.note: to hit repeatedly is to flog
a club is a heavy stick

explanation.surface: A chauffeur strikes back with a heavy cudgel.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is the golfing implement used for long tee shots.

clue.text: Maintain the usual standard though short of time

indicators.note: lacking, so that word is taken out

parts.note: the average is the normal or typical level
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone keeps up normal standards despite being pressed for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or state firmly.

definitions.meaning: to quote is to state a price for a job
tags are quotations or familiar sayings

explanation.definitionFit: A builder quotes an estimate; tags are quotations, phrases borrowed from elsewhere.

definitions.meaning: to compensate, as in '... for lost time'

explanation.definitionFit: To make up for something is to offset it; one's make-up is one's character.

clue.text: Engage in undertaking with no purchase required

indicators.note: without, so that part is dropped

parts.note: an enterprise is a venture or undertaking
purchase means leverage, a prise

explanation.surface: A competition says you can take part without buying anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' looks like buying; it is leverage, PRISE. 'with no' removes it from ENTERPRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter into an activity is to take part in it.

parts.note: a missing word from Jaques's seven ages of man speech in As You Like It, describing an old man's stockings from his younger days

explanation.walkthrough: The line is 'His youthful hose, well saved, a world too wide / For his shrunk shank' from Shakespeare's As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the stockings worn in the old man's young days.

definitions.meaning: the way something is handled, as in 'rough handling'

explanation.definitionFit: Usage means established custom and also the manner of handling something.

clue.text: To incline to the left is initially tempting

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: only the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Leaning towards the left is at first attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that lists leans or tilts to one side.

definitions.meaning: ... House is a play by George Bernard Shaw, so this word plus house names a play

explanation.walkthrough: Playhouse looks like a theatre; it is the play Heartbreak House.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's play is titled with this word plus House; the word itself means deep sorrow.

clue.text: Resent request, roughly made, to hold a horse

parts.note: to beg is to request

indicators.note: the first word contains the second

parts.note: something roughly made is rude, crude
G is short for gee, or gee-gee, a horse

explanation.surface: Someone resents a crude request to hold onto a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge is to envy or resent something given to another.

definitions.meaning: ... Carton is the hero of Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities
a city in New South Wales

explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's character is named Sydney Carton; Sydney is Australia's largest city.
